title: GPU edge lab triage journal — ECC/NVLink intermittent reboots
content:
Summary:

Short background: Over the past 10 days we've observed 4 intermittent reboots in the GPU edge lab rack (rack-e2) where nodes powered by A100-class cards spontaneously rebooted during medium-load workloads (inference benches and througput tests). Symptoms: sudden kernel panic or machine reboot, dmesg showing repeated NVLink/PCIe link-reset warnings and growing ECC single-bit error counts immediately before the failure. This doc is a running triage journal and an initial runbook draft to make recurring investigations faster.

Observed pattern (high level):
- Workload: multi-client inference (batch sizes 8–32), sustained 40–60% GPU util, occasional 1–2s peak memory usage bursts (kv-cache warmups).
- Preceding logs: increasing single-bit ECC counts on GPU 0 and 1 during the hour prior.
- NVLink messages: kernel log shows nvlink link down/up transitions, followed by driver reset.
- Crash: kernel panic referencing NVRM or kworker backtrace, sometimes an Oops with stack showing nvidia_uvm or nvidia_drm call. Reboots are immediate (no graceful shutdown).
- Environmental: nodes are in edge lab (non-production), mixed firmware across nodes, not all cards uniformly updated.

Evidence collected (representative snippets):
- dmesg around time T: 
  "[12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00.0): 79, PID=0, GPU has fallen off the bus.
  [12345.678945] nvlink: nvlink: link 0 down
  [12345.679012] nvlink: nvlink: reset link 0
  [12345.679123] kworker/3:3: segfault at 0 ip nvidia_uvm+0x12f7f sp ..."

- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.uncorrected.single_bit --format=csv shows monotonic climb prior to event (0 -> 42 over ~45 minutes on affected GPUs).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) ECC accumulation triggering intermittent hardware/firmware protective reset when combined with NVLink retries. Single-bit ECC is high but not necessarily fatal, but pattern suggests persistent errors correlating with thermal or power instability.
2) NVLink firmware/driver mismatch causing repeated link reinitialization which triggers an NVRM Xid (79) and subsequent kernel panic.
3) Slightly loose NVLink bridge or cable in a subset of cards; mechanical cause -> link flaps under vibration/thermal expansion.
4) PCIe/BIOS power management (ASPM) interacting poorly with driver under our kernel (6.6.x) leading to link resets.

Immediate triage checklist (to run when an edge lab node reboots):
- Confirm node: hostname, rack, slot, job ids that were running.
- Collect boot logs (persisted): /var/log/syslog, /var/log/kern.log, journalctl -b -1.
- Dump dmesg from previous boot (if persisted) and current boot.
- Run nvidia-smi -q -d ECC, NVLINK, POWER, FB_MEMORY to capture counters and thermal/power state.
- Collect driver version: modinfo nvidia | grep ^version and cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version.
- Save kernel oops: /var/crash or kdump if active. If kdump not active, try to capture using netconsole for next repro.
- If possible, preserve the machine (don’t auto-reapply jobs) — cordon/mark node as investigating.

Commands/examples used during triage:
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,uuid,driver_version,pcie.link.gen.current,temperature.gpu,pstate,ecc.errors.corrected.single_bit,ecc.errors.uncorrected.single_bit --format=csv
- dmesg --ctime | egrep -i "nvlink|NVRM|Xid|nvidia|kernel panic|oops|gpu" | tail -n 200
- journalctl -k -b -1 --no-pager | sed -n '1,300p' > /tmp/previous-boot-kern.log
- /usr/local/bin/cuda-memtest --duration 20m (lab-only; small stress test for memory ECC)

Quick findings from one repro (node rack-e2-b03, 2026-03-09 02:46 UTC):
- Driver: 535.54; CUDA 12.2 runtime.
- NVLink firmware: mixed across cards (FW 2.5.1 on GPU0, 2.6.0 on GPU1).
- ECC stats: GPU0 corrected single-bit errors rose from 0 to 56 in 38 minutes; GPU1 to 12.
- dmesg: repeated "nvlink: link 1 down" events ~every 3–6 minutes for the preceding hour; final sequence: NVLink link down -> NVRM Xid 79 -> kworker OOPS -> immediate reboot.
- Temperature: 68C avg under load (within spec).
- Power draw: small spikes aligned with NVLink reset but nothing out of budget.

Interim mitigations applied to lab nodes (what we did):
- Cordoned affected nodes in k8s and moved long-running jobs to other racks.
- Disabled aggressive power management (set pcie_aspm=off via kernel boot arg on repro candidate) — no repro after change for 24h but sample size small.
- Forced consistent NVLink firmware on a 2-card set (updated both to 2.6.0), observed reduced link flaps during controlled stress.
- Hardware inspection: reseated NVLink bridges on 3/4 suspect cards; one had visible oxidation on connector pins -> flagged for RMA.

Runbook draft (play-by-play for SRE oncall):
1) Immediate: mark node as investigating: kubectl cordon <node> ; annotate with issue id.
2) Collect logs: run the commands listed above and upload to /shared/triage/gpu-edge/<node>/YYYYMMDD-HHMM.
3) Quick triage: if ECC uncorrected errors > 0 or corrected single-bit delta > 100 in last hour, tag as high-priority.
4) If NVLink link flap messages present (nvlink link down/up), try to repro in bench: run gpu-burn + nvlink heavy comms test (e.g., inter-gpu memcpy loops) for 30m.
5) If repro succeeds: isolate power/thermal/bridge checks; take photos and note firmware versions.
6) If repro does not occur: escalate to hardware team to schedule deeper hardware burn-in and RMA candidate identification.
7) For every reboot with NVRM Xid 79: open a vendor support case and attach driver logs, dumps, and last 1h of ECC counts.

Data collection improvements (short list):
- Enable kdump on all edge lab nodes and configure automatic crashkernel capture to central storage.
- Configure persistent NVLink/ECC counters export to Prometheus (scrape nvidia-smi at 30s during tests) and alert on single-bit slope > 10/min or uncorrected > 0.
- Add nvlink firmware/driver version metadata to node labels so we can quickly query fleet parity.
- Add a small netconsole capture on 2 repro candidates for kernel oops live capture to central system.

Follow-up action items (owners & ETA):
- Aisha: collate the 4 incidents into a single timeline + upload full logs to JIRA-GPU-5123 (ETA 2026-03-15).
- Luca: finish NVLink firmware parity job to update all lab nodes to 2.6.0 and run 24h burn-in (ETA 2026-03-18).
- Priya: enable kdump and netconsole on a pair of repro candidates and document capture procedures (ETA 2026-03-14).
- Ethan: run a kernel boot-flag matrix (ASPM on/off, pcie_aspm=off, nvme.noacpi?) on two nodes to check for stability differences (ETA 2026-03-20).
- Zoe: schedule vendor hardware case for card with oxidized connector and track RMA (ETA initial case 2026-03-13).

Longer-term proposals (to discuss in SRE weekly):
- Fleet-level policy: require NVLink firmware parity and driver+firmware compatibility gating for Dedicated/private rollouts.
- Automated ECC slope detection: incorporate into Optimize recommendations to suggest reduced batch sizes or routing away from noisy GPUs when slope triggers.
- Investigation into whether certain workloads (specific token-length distributions or prefix-cache patterns) correlate with spike in ECC events.

Notes/loose thoughts (scratchpad):
- I suspect combination of firmware mismatch + persistent corrected ECC indicates a hardware fault that becomes visible under NVLink stress. The driver reset may be a symptom, not the root cause.
- For next repro pass, try disabling NVLink (if possible) and see if crash disappears — that isolates cross-GPU fabric.
- Need to be careful with aggressive kdump in lab; it can mask immediate reboots. Netconsole is less intrusive and should be primary for live captures.

Appendix: Useful commands + quick-copy snippets
- Save dmesg to central:
  mkdir -p /shared/triage/gpu-edge/$HOSTNAME && dmesg --ctime -T > /shared/triage/gpu-edge/$HOSTNAME/dmesg-$(date -Iseconds).log
- ECC query (CSV): 
  nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,serial,ecc.errors.corrected.single_bit,ecc.errors.uncorrected.single_bit --format=csv -f /shared/triage/gpu-edge/$HOSTNAME/ecc-$(date -Iseconds).csv
- Quick NVLink status: 
  for dev in /sys/class/nvlink/*; do echo $dev; cat $dev/link_state; cat $dev/remote_link_state; done > /shared/triage/gpu-edge/$HOSTNAME/nvlink-states-$(date -Iseconds).log

End of draft.

-- Aisha (SRE)

Revision history:
- 2026-03-11: initial notes and first repro investigation.
- 2026-03-12: added runbook checklist and action items after firmware parity test.
